summary_en: Daiki Axis raised full-year dividend guidance for fiscal 2026 to 26 yen per share from 24 yen, a 2 yen increase from the prior year, comprising an interim dividend of 12 yen and a year-end dividend of 14 yen (up 2 yen), following upward revisions to operating and net profit forecasts driven by improved cost management and price adjustments.
title_en: Notice of Revision to Full-Year Consolidated Business Forecast and Revision to Year-End Dividend Forecast (Dividend Increase)
translation_en_brief:
Daiki Axis revised its full-year dividend forecast for fiscal year 2026 (January 1 to December 31, 2026) to 26 yen per share, up 2 yen from the prior fiscal year. The revised guidance comprises an interim dividend of 12 yen (unchanged) and a year-end dividend of 14 yen (up 2 yen from the previously announced 12 yen). This revision follows upward adjustments to consolidated earnings forecasts made the same day.

The company raised its operating profit forecast by 150 million yen to 1,600 million yen and attributable net profit by 260 million yen to 800 million yen, primarily due to improved operational performance in the third quarter and successful implementation of price adjustments to offset continued cost pressures from Middle East-related supply chain impacts. The company maintains its full-year revenue forecast at 50,000 million yen.

The company stated that its dividend policy balances stable profit returns to shareholders with sustained business growth, determined by considering consolidated earnings, payout ratio, and retained earnings on a period-by-period basis. The 2 yen increase in annual dividend reflects management's confidence in the upward earnings revision and commitment to shareholder returns.
